speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe exactly what the vertigo feels like—does the room appear to be spinning around you, or do you feel lightheaded and faint? Additionally, have you experienced any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or nausea accompanying these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Since the episode was brief and triggered by lying down, I need to know if the vertigo returns when you change your head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up. Do you have any history of migraines, or have you noticed any weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking during or after the episode?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the spinning sensation recur specifically when you roll over in bed or look up, and have you noticed any hearing loss or ringing in your ears? I also need to know if you have any history of migraines or if you experienced any weakness, numbness, or speech difficulties during the episode.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the brief duration of the episode and its association with lying down, I need to rule out central causes. Do you have any history of migraines, and did you experience any neurological symptoms like weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking during the episode?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headaches, hearing loss, tinnitus, loss of consciousness or neurological deficits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture is highly suggestive of Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) given the brief, position-triggered episodes and lack of neurological or auditory symptoms. I will now perform a physical exam to confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver
